Claim 1 (currently amended): A method for treating an ocular condition, the method comprising: administering to the interior of an eye a composition comprising a therapeutically effective amount of a macromolecular anti-angiogenic component (MAAC) to a mammal suffering from an ocular condition, wherein the composition also comprises a viscosity inducing component in an amount effective to increase the viscosity of the composition to a viscosity at 25°C of at least 10 cps at a shear rate of about 0.1/second, wherein said viscosity inducing component is injectable into the vitreous of a mammalian eye without permanently diminishing visual acuity.

Claim 5 (currently amended): The method of claim 1 wherein a symptom of the ocular condition is angiogenesis and the MAAC comprises a direct or indirect inhibitor of vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) activity. 

Claim 6 (cancelled): The method of claim 5 wherein the MAAC comprises an agent selected from the group consisting of a nucleic acid (an oligonucleotide) and a polypeptide.

Claim 14 (currently amended): The method of claim 1 wherein said MAAC comprises a polypeptide selected from the group consisting of an angiogenesis inhibitor. 

Claim 16 (currently amended): The method of claim 14 wherein said protein comprises a therapeutic agent selected from the group consisting of bevacizumab. 

Claim 20 (currently amended): The method of claim 1 wherein said viscosity inducing component comprises a hyaluronic acid. 

Claim 24 (currently amended): The method of claim 1 wherein said viscosity inducing component has a viscosity of at least 10 cps at a shear rate of 0.1/second at 25°C. 

Claim 36 (currently amended): The method of claim 1 wherein said condition is selected from the group consisting of macular degeneration.
